overview: The two possible allele combinations at a single gene locus, with real consequences for which trait is expressed.
genZNote: Homozygous: matching socks. Heterozygous: one of each, dominant one wins the outfit.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Having two identical alleles for a given gene (e.g. AA or aa).
aspects.valueB: Having two different alleles for a given gene (e.g. Aa).

aspects.label: Allele Combination
aspects.valueA: Both alleles are the same — either homozygous dominant (AA) or homozygous recessive (aa).
aspects.valueB: One dominant and one recessive allele present together (Aa).

aspects.label: Phenotype Expressed
aspects.valueA: Homozygous dominant expresses the dominant trait; homozygous recessive expresses the recessive trait.
aspects.valueB: Expresses the dominant trait if simple dominance applies, or an intermediate/blended trait under incomplete dominance.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: BB (homozygous dominant, brown eyes) or bb (homozygous recessive, blue eyes).
aspects.valueB: Bb — carries one brown allele and one blue allele, but expresses brown eyes if brown is dominant.

aspects.label: Carrier Status for Recessive Conditions
aspects.valueA: Homozygous recessive individuals are affected by recessive genetic disorders.
aspects.valueB: Heterozygous individuals are typically unaffected carriers of a recessive disorder allele.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Two identical alleles at a locus.
aspects.valueB: Two different alleles at a locus.
